Decentralized Infrastructure

Zero Downtime: Routstr Sunsets Last Official Node as Network Turns 100% Community-Run

Six weeks after quietly decommissioning api.routstr.com, the routing project confirms full client autonomy across Nostr without a central server dependency.

By Staff

For protocols whose defining promise is resilience against capture, centralized bootstrap servers have long remained an awkward compromise. Today, routing protocol Routstr confirmed that the network has quietly crossed a significant milestone: its last official server, api.routstr.com, was retired a month and a half ago, and the network transitioned entirely to community-run infrastructure without a flicker of interruption.

We Sunset Our Official Node. Zero Downtime. the project declared, noting that in the six weeks since shutting down the official endpoint, Nobody noticed a thing. Instead of pinging a core server, client software now coordinates peer discovery natively across relays: routstrd and routstr-sdk discover nodes on Nostr and pick the cheapest one for you automatically. The result is a system insulated from platform capture: No one can rugpull you. No one can capture you. Your client truly works for you. Project maintainers added: We're removing the team as a dependency. routstr

Sovereign Hardware

Legacy Mode on Passport Prime: Open-Source KeyOS Bridges Existing Wallets

Foundation brings open-source Ledger apps to its flagship hardware, allowing seed migration without moving balances on-chain.

By Staff

Hardware manufacturer Foundation announced the public beta of Legacy Mode for its Passport Prime device, aiming to streamline the migration path for users seeking fully open-source hardware without breaking existing accounts. Legacy Mode is live in beta on Passport Prime. the team announced, adding that KeyOS has incorporated supported open-source applications to enable USB connectivity with multi-asset browser wallets: We’ve brought supported open source Ledger apps to KeyOS, our open source operating system. For users concerned with transaction fees and privacy, Restore your existing recovery phrase directly on Passport Prime and keep your accounts for supported assets. The migration preserves ledger state: Same addresses. Same balances. Same transaction history. Nothing moves on-chain. Foundation

Dispatches & Infrastructure

Protocol Economics

Relay Economics: fiatjaf on the Limits of Altruism

By Staff

The chronic question of who finances the storage and bandwidth of Nostr relays resurfaced today in a series of incisive reflections from protocol creator fiatjaf, who warned against the expectation that volunteer server operators should bear unbounded compute loads.

Why would a business pay for a relay either? That doesn't make sense either. If they can write to nos.lol for free. fiatjaf noted, observing that commercial entities and automated bots routinely treat public relays as open dumping grounds. To some people Nostr is defined as a collection of free servers anyone can write anything to, as long as that anything is formatted as a weird JSON string with a meaningless signature. Confronting large web-of-trust spiders that maintain permanent connections to ingest firehoses of unrelated traffic, he questioned the architectural premise: Do you really want to ingest millions of events from people who don't even know your relay exists? fiatjaf

Privacy & Custody

The Wrench Hazard: Ungovernable on KYC Leaks and Ashigaru

By Staff

Recent corporate data breaches stemming from fraudulent government subpoenas prompted sharp reflections on the physical risks generated by centralized compliance databases. Host Ungovernable outlined the stark threat model facing exchange customers whose withdrawal histories are compromised.

KYC: kill your customer. he warned. An attacker now holds your personal information and your Bitcoin withdrawal history in the same file. They do not have to guess whether you are worth robbing, and they do not have to guess where you live. Crucially, he noted that this exposure was systematically imposed: None of this was a choice anybody made. The data existed because a regulator required it to be collected, from people who had no way to opt out, in the name of protecting them. Turning to practical remediation, he highlighted the automated cold-storage sweep in Ashigaru Desktop: Mix To is the feature more people should know about. Ungovernable

Software Security

Tor Advisory: Bisq 2 Rolls Out Mandatory v2.1.13 Patch

By Bisq

The Bisq peer-to-peer trading network issued an urgent update for all Bisq 2 desktop users following an upstream security vulnerability discovered in the Tor anonymity network.

Bisq 2 v2.1.13 is released the project notified users, warning that the release addresses an essential network component: This is an important security update which includes the latest Tor security release. Because peer-to-peer settlement relies entirely on onion routing, Updating to this version is required to continue trading. Traders are urged to upgrade before opening new offers on the book. Bisq

Marginalia

Curated by Gigi

Gigi highlighted several acute reflections from Constant's essay on the structural traps of centralized internet platforms:

Looking back at the trajectory of the commercial web, Constant observed how time and space were condensed to irrelevance and noted that while Going viral leveled a playing field otherwise determined by privileged access, the underlying architecture soon devoured its users: the platform way of organizing ourselves on the internet created a whole list of problems of its own.

Yet critique alone achieves little without alternative architectures: Any complaint is only relevant in light of a solution. Constant
